newsitem.title: POLAND: KACZMAREK MULLS BECOMING POLISH ECONOMY MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: KACZMAREK MULLS BECOMING POLISH ECONOMY MINISTER.

text.p: Poland's former privatisation minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek, now a deputy treasury minister, said on Thursday he was considering becoming economy minister when the portfolio is created in January.
"I have moved closer to agreeing to that," PAP news agency quoted Kaczmarek as saying.
The economy ministry will replace the current industry and foreign trade portfolios as of January 1, 1997, under a sweeping reorganisation of government ministries launched earlier this year.

Kaczmarek, considered one of the most pro-reform politicians in the ruling left-wing coalition, lost his job as the head of the privatisation ministry in October when it was transformed into the treasury portfolio.

Under an agreement between the two coalition parties, the treasury ministry went to the smaller Polish Peasant Party (PSL) and the economy ministry to the larger ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).
SLD's Kaczmarek is often criticised by the PSL, where many politicians are hostile to privatisation and favour protectionist policies.
The economy ministry will devise industrial and trade policy.
Unlike the current industry ministry, it will not control state-owned companies, which will fall under the supervision of the treasury ministry.
